From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge deal team. All Seller material treated as the counterparty's untrusted draft and tested against our playbook. Where our playbook has a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written authority, I note that **no such authority has been given** and I have not assumed it.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (our opening position). 20% is a conditional fallback only, and only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The Seller has landed exactly on our unauthorised fallback – do not accept it without Amelia Frost's written sign-off referencing SPA-003.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's package is 5x our thresholds and converts a tipping basket into a deductible, which permanently writes off the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months; plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Reject the "applies to all Claims" sweep (see also N-014).
- **Recommendation:** **Counter at 24 months and strike the catch-all sentence.** 18 months is our unauthorised fallback, and the sweep would drag Title, Tax, IP and indemnity claims under the general time bar.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery on defective title at 20% of a AUD 24m price and time-bar it at 18 months.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature". No fraud carve-out is offered.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable on our side.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out.** This is a hard-line item – no one on the buyer side has authority to trade it, and a clause purporting to cap fraud is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. [1.4] denies every admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only (fair, specific, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter). Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1]–[1.2] and replace with a fair-disclosure standard tied to the specific disclosures in sections 2–10.** Whole-data-room disclosure would deem us to know everything in DD-002–DD-012 and gut the warranties, particularly in combination with Cl 8.3.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any residual qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals (and seller knowledge qualifiers to named seller persons after reasonable enquiry) and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete Cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge plus whole-data-room disclosure is a three-layer bar that would make most warranty claims unwinnable.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 Sept 2026.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion condition requiring (a) effective written Bluefen consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 **and** (b) evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, both delivered before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a ~30% / ~AUD 3.6m revenue customer.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make this a hard CP with a conditions-satisfied deliverable.** Bluefen is roughly 30% of FY26 revenue and the Seller's own letter admits neither the consent nor the condition evidence exists yet.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter §3 confirms not repaid and no discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** We would otherwise own an encumbered company with a bank holding a change-of-control trigger (DD-003 cl 8.1) and no contractual path to discharge.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow – DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter §5 confirms exclusion from the funds flow and silence on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals as applicable) as an express line item in the funds flow, either deducted from price as a Debt-like item or paid by the Seller at/before Completion. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; add a specific funds-flow line for AUD 420,000 + on-costs, seller-funded.** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless once the Company we are buying is the employer paying the bonus.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter §4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is **not** independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment on file.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering loss arising from any failure of title to or infringement claim over the SOW3 Project Materials (and related Ironquay deliverables), not merely the fee amount, while preserving the cure path (pay the SOW3 fee → trigger cl 7.3 transfer → confirmatory assignment). The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and add a Completion deliverable of either (a) cleared-payment evidence + confirmatory IP assignment or (b) a seller-funded cure.** The commercial risk is losing title to project IP, not the AUD 180,000 invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter §6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no loss amount stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs and evidence; complete the investigation; seller covenant to update the Buyer through Completion and to provide an investigation report pre-Completion; specific warranty/indemnity that any notification, regulatory or third-party cost arising from the incident is for the Seller. Do **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; insert preservation, investigation, update and specific-indemnity provisions.** The facts are unresolved on the Seller's own account, so the price of materiality should sit with the Seller, not be prejudged either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter §8 does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment, not automatic treatment. Require the Seller to disclose timing, scope, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-paid; reserve the right to treat accrued or non-terminable pre-Completion obligations as Debt-like. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as a conclusion; request the underlying renewal terms and reserve the Debt/Working Capital treatment pending review.** The Seller's own letter declines to say these are ordinary course, so neither side should assume it.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 sweep ("any limitation... applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") plus Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") plus Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, Debt, bonuses, leakage) and covenants each in a separate, expressly ring-fenced regime. No general-regime catch-all that overrides them by default.
- **Recommendation:** **Strike every "all Claims" / "unless expressly stated otherwise" default and reverse the drafting so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.** The Seller has used three separate clauses to achieve the same hidden override – treat them as one issue and close all three.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter §10 concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and does not assert buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances and seller authority: ASIC extract/historical company search, PPSR search against Company and Seller, inspection of share certificates and transfer history, Seller board/shareholder authorities, and confirmation Riverlark's security (if over shares) is released. DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as title evidence; run independent searches and require title/authority deliverables at Completion.** An internal register maintained by the seller's company cannot verify the seller's own title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above" (i.e. 20% cap / 18 months / AUD 250,000 deductible basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**. Each needs its own regime (cap, duration tied to assessment periods for Tax, and a tax indemnity), to be negotiated. We do not assume unlimited liability and we do not assume resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" statement in writing and record Tax and IP as open items.** Silence now risks the Seller treating our general-regime mark-up as implicit acceptance of their Tax/IP treatment.

---

## Cross-cutting observations

1. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter undercuts its Update.** On Bluefen (§2), Riverlark (§3), Ironquay (§4), bonuses (§5), the incident (§6), Sandbar (§8) and title (§10), the letter expressly declines to confirm the facts the Update treats as resolved. Quote these back in our cover note.
2. **Three structural devices compound each other:** whole-data-room disclosure (N-006) + discoverability knowledge bar (N-007) + "all Claims" sweeps (N-014). Any one would be damaging; together they would make the warranty package close to illusory. They should be rejected as a package.
3. **Two items land on our unauthorised fallbacks (N-001 at 20%, N-003 at 18 months).** Flag to Amelia Frost that the Seller has anchored exactly there; no written authority exists for either and none should be inferred from this review.
4. **Two items require hard Completion deliverables rather than drafting fixes:** Bluefen consent + conditions evidence (N-008) and Riverlark payout + releases (N-009). Both involve change-of-control triggers on ~AUD 3.2–3.6m exposures.
5. **Nothing in this review assumes a confirmed breach, loss or demand on DD-006, or a verified AUD 180,000 on Ironquay** – both remain factual questions for the Seller to answer.

Happy to turn this into a formal mark-up table or an issues list for the next call with Harbourglass's counsel.

- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; insert preservation, investigation, update and specific-indemnity provisions.** The facts are unresolved on the Seller's own account, so the price of materiality should sit with the Seller, not be prejudged either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter §8 does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment, not automatic treatment. Require the Seller to disclose timing, scope, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-paid; reserve the right to treat accrued or non-terminable pre-Completion obligations as Debt-like. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as a conclusion; request the underlying renewal terms and reserve the Debt/Working Capital treatment pending review.** The Seller's own letter declines to say these are ordinary course, so neither side should assume it.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 sweep ("any limitation... applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") plus Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") plus Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, Debt, bonuses, leakage) and covenants each in a separate, expressly ring-fenced regime. No general-regime catch-all that overrides them by default.
- **Recommendation:** **Strike every "all Claims" / "unless expressly stated otherwise" default and reverse the drafting so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.** The Seller has used three separate clauses to achieve the same hidden override – treat them as one issue and close all three.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter §10 concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and does not assert buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances and seller authority: ASIC extract/historical company search, PPSR search against Company and Seller, inspection of share certificates and transfer history, Seller board/shareholder authorities, and confirmation Riverlark's security (if over shares) is released. DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as title evidence; run independent searches and require title/authority deliverables at Completion.** An internal register maintained by the seller's company cannot verify the seller's own title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above" (i.e. 20% cap / 18 months / AUD 250,000 deductible basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**. Each needs its own regime (cap, duration tied to assessment periods for Tax, and a tax indemnity), to be negotiated. We do not assume unlimited liability and we do not assume resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" statement in writing and record Tax and IP as open items.** Silence now risks the Seller treating our general-regime mark-up as implicit acceptance of their Tax/IP treatment.

## Cross-cutting observations

1. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter undercuts its Update.** On Bluefen (§2), Riverlark (§3), Ironquay (§4), bonuses (§5), the incident (§6), Sandbar (§8) and title (§10), the letter expressly declines to confirm the facts the Update treats as resolved. Quote these back in our cover note.
2. **Three structural devices compound each other:** whole-data-room disclosure (N-006) + discoverability knowledge bar (N-007) + "all Claims" sweeps (N-014). Any one would be damaging; together they would make the warranty package close to illusory. They should be rejected as a package.
3. **Two items land on our unauthorised fallbacks (N-001 at 20%, N-003 at 18 months).** Flag to Amelia Frost that the Seller has anchored exactly there; no written authority exists for either and none should be inferred from this review.
4. **Two items require hard Completion deliverables rather than drafting fixes:** Bluefen consent + conditions evidence (N-008) and Riverlark payout + releases (N-009). Both involve change-of-control triggers on ~AUD 3.2–3.6m exposures.
5. **Nothing in this review assumes a confirmed breach, loss or demand on DD-006, or a verified AUD 180,000 on Ironquay** – both remain factual questions for the Seller to answer.
